Snow Report

Monday November 16 at 8:36 AM

Couple Inches Closer to Opening Day

The waiting game continues, though we've finally got a little more to show for all the staring at the sky. Our first countable snowfall of the season arrived over the weekend, with up to 8 inches at the summit on Saturday, November 14th. Not quite enough to start waxing poetic about winter, but certainly enough to remind us what we're waiting for.

Meanwhile, our Snowmaking Team has been making some serious progress. Guns have been running all weekend top to bottom on the Jet, as well as lower Montrealer to the Wiggle, pushing 2,000 gallons per minute up the mountain. That's our system running at full capacity, and we'll be keeping things going through the day today while temperatures cooperate.

The forecast gets a little less accommodating starting Tuesday as we lose the colder air, though some low-level inversions could linger in the morning. Milder, quieter weather looks to carry us through much of the week before a possible quick cold front Friday brings cooler temperatures Saturday. A stronger cold front is looking possible early next week as we head toward Thanksgiving and our anticipated Opening Day.

For now, we're still patiently waiting for Friday, November 27th, and our annual Day for the Devoted. Eight inches on the summit and a weekend of snowguns running wide open have certainly helped the cause. Now we just need November to keep up its end of the arrangement.

Get the full details on Opening Weekend and Day for the Devoted.
